en: The Philippines is an archipelago of 7,641 islands, significantly more than the previously recorded count of 7,107 islands.
Mount Apo stands 2,954 meters tall, making it the highest peak in the Philippines, towering over Mount Pulag's 2,928 meters.
Mount Mayon has erupted over 50 times, making it the most active volcano in the Philippines, far exceeding the eruption count of Mount Pinatubo.
The Cagayan River stretches 505 kilometers, making it the longest river in the Philippines, much longer than the 25-kilometer Pasig River.
Laguna de Bay covers 911 square kilometers, making it the largest lake in the Philippines, nearly three times bigger than Lake Lanao.
Luzon is the largest island in the Philippines, covering 109,965 square kilometers, which is roughly half of the country's total land area.
The Sierra Madre spans 540 kilometers along eastern Luzon, making it the longest mountain range in the Philippines, much longer than the Cordillera Central.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River stretches 8.2 kilometers underground, making it the longest navigable underground river in the Philippines and one of the longest globally.
The Galathea Depth in the Philippine Trench reaches 10,540 meters, making it the deepest point in the Philippines and the third deepest globally.
Aliwagwag Falls drops a total of 340 meters across 84 cascades, making it the highest waterfall in the Philippines, significantly taller than Maria Cristina Falls.
Palawan is the largest province in the Philippines, covering 14,649 square kilometers, which is significantly larger than the second-largest province, Isabela.
Baguio City receives an average annual rainfall of 3,800 millimeters, making it one of the wettest cities, receiving nearly double the rainfall of Manila.
